Annual site energy consumption per upgraded dwelling unit Table 5 shows the annual energy consumption savings percentage per upgraded dwelling unit. As discussed earlier, most savings were observed in heating and cooling end uses. However, there is only a small change in hot water-related end uses. When both the water heater and ducts are in the same place (e.g., unheated basement or attic), hot water energy consumption can be affected slightly due to reduced heat transfer from the ducts. If the water heater is in the attic, it can also be affected by improved attic floor insulation. Additional details are available in the duct sealing and attic floor insulation documentation (Lou & Liu, 2025) (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025b). Furthermore, indoor temperature changes also influence hot water energy use. Overall, the impact on hot water energy consumption is less than 0.2%. There is also a very small change in appliance electricity use, primarily for refrigerators. Refrigerators work by transferring heat from the interior to the surrounding air. When the surrounding air is cooler, a refrigerator operates more efficiently and uses less energy. The average indoor temperature over the year increased slightly from 71.28°F to 71.46°F. This slight increase in temperature results in a minor increase in refrigerator energy use. However, the impact is negligible—the change in appliance electricity consumption is 0.21%. 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
